pr.body:
Changes:
- Initializes unified storage when the `ResourceServer` is created, instead of doing it inside the first gRPC call it receives. This was causing context cancelled errors since the index takes too long to build within the context of the gRPC call.
- Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down.
- Improves index build speed using finer grain locking when writing the index cache. We were locking the whole `BuildIndex` function, which was slowing things down when building many namespaces with high concurrency.

Notes for reviewer:
- Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?
pr.title: Unified Storage: Init at startup, fix traces, and speed up indexing

raw_findings.body: Both callers independently build the index; file-backed builds can conflict while opening the same Bleve directory, and memory-backed callers can receive different snapshots while the last completed build replaces the cache entry.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent cache misses are no longer coalesced, producing index-open errors or inconsistent search results.
raw_findings.impact: Both callers independently build the index; file-backed builds can conflict while opening the same Bleve directory, and memory-backed callers can receive different snapshots while the last completed build replaces the cache entry.
raw_findings.root_cause: The function-wide build mutex was removed without replacing it with synchronization for concurrent builds of the same cache key.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add per-key in-flight coordination around the GetIndex/build sequence, rechecking the cache after acquiring the key lock so only one build runs for each namespaced resource.
raw_findings.title: Concurrent cache misses can build the same index simultaneously
raw_findings.trigger: Two concurrent searches request an uncached namespaced resource, causing both calls to pass GetIndex with nil and enter BuildIndex at the same time.

finding.body: Both callers independently build the index; file-backed builds can conflict while opening the same Bleve directory, and memory-backed callers can receive different snapshots while the last completed build replaces the cache entry.
finding.failure_mode: Concurrent cache misses are no longer coalesced, producing index-open errors or inconsistent search results.
finding.impact: Both callers independently build the index; file-backed builds can conflict while opening the same Bleve directory, and memory-backed callers can receive different snapshots while the last completed build replaces the cache entry.
finding.root_cause: The function-wide build mutex was removed without replacing it with synchronization for concurrent builds of the same cache key.
finding.suggested_fix: Add per-key in-flight coordination around the GetIndex/build sequence, rechecking the cache after acquiring the key lock so only one build runs for each namespaced resource.
finding.title: Concurrent cache misses can build the same index simultaneously
finding.trigger: Two concurrent searches request an uncached namespaced resource, causing both calls to pass GetIndex with nil and enter BuildIndex at the same time.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch removes lines 88-89 (b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()) from BuildIndex, but the candidate claims this is on the LEFT side line 88. However, examining the actual code flow: GetIndex at lines 60-68 uses RLock for cache reads, and BuildIndex at lines 137-139 still acquires cacheMu.Lock() before writing to cache. The removed lock was at the function entry, but the cache write is still protected. The candidate's claim about 'concurrent builds of the same cache key' conflicting is speculative - the code at lines 287-306 in search.go shows getOrCreateIndex calls GetIndex first, and if nil, calls build(). The existing TODO comment at line 288-290 acknowledges this pattern needs improvement but the patch doesn't introduce a new defect - it removes redundant locking while keeping the cache-write lock.
